edit.description: `run` decides its shell and its argv refusal from a platform it is given, and the script's body runs under the direct-invocation guard `build-changelog.mjs` already carries
the win32 refusal driven off an injected platform, beside the smoke's existing source scans

summary: The smoke's win32 argv refusal is held by nothing in-tree: `run` reads `process.platform` at module load in a script whose import runs the whole smoke, so deleting the guard stays green on every lane

per.section: A fix ships the test that would have caught it

acceptance: the smoke's step runner is importable without running the smoke and takes the platform it decides on, so the win32 refusal is driven by the suite on the posix lane rather than measured against an out-of-tree copy
tests: the smoke step runner refuses an argv cmd.exe would re-parse when the platform it is given is win32
importing the install smoke module does not run the smoke
notes: Off note THE-SMOKE-SHELL-REFUSES-AN-ARGV-IT-WOULD-REWRITE, item 1; 7a411920's body names the no-test exception, whose condition is false. Scoped to the tree's own precedent rather than the note's proposed new module: `scripts/build-changelog.mjs` exports its functions behind an `import.meta.url` vs resolved `process.argv[1]` guard (`:317`), which is what the suite drives at `tests/build-changelog.test.ts:16`. `IS_WIN` (`:60`) feeds `run` twice — the refusal (`:112`) and `shell:` (`:127`).
